chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah al-Hajjal, from Hafs ibn Abu Ayesha, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent one of his slaves on a need, and he was delayed. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out after him when he was delayed, and found him sleeping. So he sat by his head fanning him until he woke up. And when he woke up, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O so-and-so! By Allah, that is not for you; you sleep night and day. For you is the night, and for us, from you, is the day.'

key_terms.فُلَانٌ: so-and-so (a placeholder name used when the specific name is omitted or generic)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq demonstrate patience and kindness when his slave was late and sleeping?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) characteristic *hilm* (forbearance), demonstrating that leadership in Shia tradition is defined by patience and consideration rather than authoritarianism. By fanning the sleeping slave, the Imam modeled compassionate care, while his gentle reminder about the division of labor—night for the master, day for the servant—underscores a fair and reciprocal social contract. This narrative is frequently cited by scholars to illustrate the ethical treatment of servants and the spiritual virtue of controlling one's temper in daily interactions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Al Hajjal, from Hafs Bin Abu Ayesha who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> sent a slave of his<sup>asws</sup> regarding a need, and he was delayed. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> went out upon his footsteps (to find out) as to what had delayed him, and he<sup>asws</sup> found him sleeping. So he<sup>asws</sup> sat by his head fanning him until he woke up. So when he woke up, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘O so and so! By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, that is not for you that you sleep night and the day. For you is the night and for us<sup>asws</sup>, from you, is the day’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah al-Hajjal from Hafs ibn abu ‘A’isha who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) once sent one of his slaves for a certain work and he delayed. The Imam then went out to find why he has delayed so much. He found him sleeping. He sat near his head fanning to comfort him until he woke up. When he fully woke up, abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said to him, ‘O so and so, Allah knows, you are not supposed to do this. You sleep night and day. The night is for you to sleep and your day is for us.’”
